title: Fast on-demand Memory Mapping for Shared Memory and Disaggregated Systems
problem: Efficient synchronization of memory mapping information across processes is costly, particularly in fault-driven memory mapping models where page table walks and updates are expensive. This is critical for disaggregated and heterogeneous systems.
motivation: As systems evolve toward greater resource disaggregation and heterogeneity, shared memory export between processes requires costly page table operations. Current approaches like XPMEM incur significant overhead when establishing shared mappings.
method: The system implements a shared-memory driver inspired by XPMEM. It batches and parallelizes pinning operations (locking memory pages in place) instead of handling them one at a time, reducing synchronization overhead. When mapping to physical frame numbers—the actual memory addresses—it skips unnecessary cache-policy lookups. Through dynamic re-registration, it can expand the registered memory region without resetting existing mappings.
key_novelty: The key idea is combining parallel batched pinning (locking multiple memory pages together) with dynamic re-registration that preserves existing mappings, which eliminates redundant translation work and enables memory sharing to scale efficiently.
contributions: 13.22x reduction in cold-start memory copy over XPMEM in multi-process workloads
Techniques for avoiding redundant translation work in memory mapping
Strategies applicable to disaggregated systems including GPU disaggregation and heterogeneous memory environments
Evaluation on collective communication patterns and rapidly resizing buffers

metrics.memory_mapping_overhead_reduction: Significant reduction in page table operations
